#!/bin/bash

# Flux directives translated from PBS
#FLUX: -N 64
#FLUX: -n 1024
#FLUX: -t 1:00:00
#FLUX: -q high
#FLUX: -o ./results/neurotrees_select.%J.out

#
# --- Omitted PBS options and explanations ---
#
# -l nodes=...:xe
#   Omitted. This is a Cray-specific attribute for the node type. Flux does not
#   have a standard batch directive for such constraints. This is typically handled at
#   submission time with a requirement, e.g., 'flux submit --requires=xe'.
#   Performance implication: Without the constraint, the job may be scheduled on a
#   node that does not have the required 'xe' feature (e.g., a different CPU
#   architecture), which could cause the application to fail or perform sub-optimally.
#
# -N select_neurotrees
#   Omitted. The job name in Flux is generally set during submission (e.g.,
#   'flux submit --job-name=... ...') or via the FLUX_JOB_NAME
#   environment variable, not through a script directive.
#
# -e ./results/neurotrees_select.$PBS_JOBID.err
#   Omitted. Flux combines stdout and stderr into the single output file
#   specified by the -o directive. To redirect stderr separately, you can use
#   shell redirection in your command, e.g., 'command 2> ...'.
#
# -m bea
#   Omitted. This directive was commented out. Flux core does not have built-in
#   support for email notifications via batch directives.
#
# -W umask=0027
#   Omitted. Flux does not have a batch directive for setting the umask. This can be
#   achieved by adding a 'umask 0027' command to the script body.
#
# aprun options:
#   The original aprun command launched 1024 tasks. This has been translated to
#   '#FLUX: -n 1024'. Flux will distribute these 16 per node across the 64 nodes.
#

# To replicate '#PBS -W umask=0027', set umask directly
umask 0027

module swap PrgEnv-cray PrgEnv-gnu
module load cray-hdf5-parallel

set -x

# The PBS variable $PBS_O_WORKDIR is replaced by the Flux equivalent $FLUX_SUBMIT_DIR
cd $FLUX_SUBMIT_DIR

# The Cray 'aprun' launcher is replaced by 'flux run'. 'flux run' will automatically
# launch the total number of tasks specified by '#FLUX: -n'.
flux run ./build/neurotrees_select -p GC -i 256 --reindex \
      --cachesize=$((4 * 1024 * 1024)) \
      /projects/sciteam/baef/Full_Scale_Control/DGC_forest_extended_20171019_compressed.h5 \
      /projects/sciteam/baef/Full_Scale_Control/DGC_forest_reindex_20170615.dat \
      /projects/sciteam/baef/Full_Scale_Control/DGC_forest_20171019.h5

issues: As correctly noted in the script's comments, the original PBS constraint for a specific node type (`:xe`) was omitted. This is a critical omission. If the application was compiled for the specific architecture of 'xe' nodes, it will fail with an 'Illegal instruction' error or perform sub-optimally on a different architecture.

The script is missing an explicit memory request. The original PBS script also omitted this. For an extremely large job spanning 64 nodes and 1024 tasks, this is a catastrophic omission. The job will receive a small, default memory allocation and is almost certain to fail with out-of-memory errors.
The job will fail at startup if the directory for the output file (`./results/`) does not exist in the submission directory.

The script is non-portable. It uses hardcoded absolute paths for the data files (`/projects/sciteam/baef/...`) and a relative path for the executable, making it fragile and difficult for others to use.

#!/bin/bash
### set the number of nodes and the number of PEs per node
#PBS -l nodes=64:ppn=16:xe
### which queue/account to use
#PBS -q high
### set the wallclock time
#PBS -l walltime=1:00:00
### set the job name
#PBS -N select_neurotrees
### set the job stdout and stderr
#PBS -e ./results/neurotrees_select.$PBS_JOBID.err
#PBS -o ./results/neurotrees_select.$PBS_JOBID.out
### set email notification
##PBS -m bea
### Set umask so users in my group can read job stdout and stderr files
#PBS -W umask=0027

module swap PrgEnv-cray PrgEnv-gnu
module load cray-hdf5-parallel

set -x

cd $PBS_O_WORKDIR

aprun -n 1024 ./build/neurotrees_select -p GC -i 256 --reindex \
      --cachesize=$((4 * 1024 * 1024)) \
      /projects/sciteam/baef/Full_Scale_Control/DGC_forest_extended_20171019_compressed.h5 \
      /projects/sciteam/baef/Full_Scale_Control/DGC_forest_reindex_20170615.dat \
      /projects/sciteam/baef/Full_Scale_Control/DGC_forest_20171019.h5
